analysis: Examined EngineV2Bridge.swift (the changes are doc-comment only at lines ~124-125; the shown init, SSD/complete-store acceptance, prefix-cache evidence wiring and test seams are unchanged context) and the MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift patch. In the scheduler, the reasoning-prefix probe moves ahead of bridge.submitTokenized on the media path so a per-request stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope.scope(reasoningParser:reasoningPrefix:)) can be passed. The same scope is passed on the text path (~line 1043) and the native path (~line 1426, with reasoningPrefix nil). The patch removes two post-submit checkFirstContentDeadline() calls around the prefix computation. The probe now runs before submission, and checkFirstContentDeadline() still runs at line 788 before it. Impact is limited to availability or latency: a request could proceed past an expired first-content deadline between submit and stream construction. makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream remains in place, so the hard deadline checks are likely retained there. This is not a confidentiality or integrity regression. The stop-string scope is a correctness feature; the trust boundary is unchanged, and no changes touch the key, attestation, cache encryption, or the ssdPrefixCache/T-041 at-rest surface. Unverified from the supplied evidence: the bridge-side submitTokenized signature accepting stopStringScope and how it overrides the bridge-level default (the diff of EngineV2Bridge+Submission and ReasoningStopScope was not supplied), and whether a nil scope for native requests matches the whole generated text (a safe default). The scheduler patch excerpt was marked incomplete, so the coverage of the head is partial. No concrete security finding is supported.
